# Archetypal Architecture

This file is the index. The cards live in `resources/`, one file per family.
Read only the family you cast from, and load another only if the piece moves.

Casting starts from the situation the piece is in, not from its subject.
Order & Stability (Ruler, Creator, Caregiver) fits a piece about a standard
already standing, a craft, or a duty of care. Mastery & Risk (Hero, Outlaw,
Magician) fits action on the world: a trial, a break, a transformation.
Belonging & Connection (Everyperson, Lover, Jester) fits who is in the room:
fitting in, being chosen, being forgiven. Independence & Fulfillment
(Innocent, Sage, Explorer) fits what the reader believes or wants for
themselves. Narrative Functions (Guardian, Herald, Shapeshifter, Ally) are
turns inside a story rather than a standing voice: cast one for a gate, a
call, an ambiguity or a companion in the piece itself.

When two cards fit, cast the one whose dread the piece is actually about.
Every motive is broad enough to fit a dozen of the sixteen; the dread is what
separates them.

Keeping the voice: the voice list is the register, the lexicon is the
diction, and the never-say list is the tell. A draft that keeps the words but
loses the register is a costume.

Rules that hold across every card:

- Cast by the dread. If you cannot name what the voice fears losing, you
have picked a mood, not an archetype.
- One archetype carries a piece. A second voice in the same text reads as
drift, not range.
- The voice list outranks the lexicon. The right words in the wrong
temperature are pastiche.
- Use three of the lexicon's words before reaching outside it.
- The shadow is the same motive under fear. When a draft turns cruel,
dismissive or grandiose, name which dread is speaking.
- The forbidden phrasing is load-bearing. One "I think maybe" undoes a
sovereign paragraph.

## Order & Stability (3 cards)

Read `resources/order-stability.md` for the full card text.

| ID | Card | Dread |
|---|---|---|
| ARCH-01 | Ruler (Sovereign) | Anarchy: a decision made twice, an authority nobody recognises, a system coming apart while everyone is still talking. |
| ARCH-02 | Creator (Artist / Architect) | Sterility: derivative work, acceptable mediocrity, and a mind that has stopped imagining anything new. |
| ARCH-03 | Caregiver (Nurturer / Steward) | Neglect: harm that could have been prevented, and a person left to carry it alone. |
